purpose: Evidence ledger for a direct prescribed axial heat-release closure. It authorizes model interfaces and functional forms only; it does not freeze a formal reactive case parameter set.

sources.citation: Ruifeng Cao, Yue Lu, Daren Yu, Juntao Chang et al., Study on influencing factors of combustion mode transition boundary for a scramjet engine based on one-dimensional model, Aerospace Science and Technology 96 (2020) 105590.
confirmed_claims: The study uses a one-dimensional scramjet model to investigate combustion-mode transition boundary.
Heat-release distribution in the combustor is explicitly identified as an influencing factor on the mode-transition boundary.
Combustor area profile, wall temperature/roughness, and inflow air composition are additional influencing factors.

sources.citation: Kaiyan Jin, Jianbin Li, Lin Zhang, Jianhan Liang, Xiaodong Cai, Experimental study on heat release distribution during supersonic combustion, Combustion and Flame 287 (2026) 114876.
sources.role: direct experimental heat-release-distribution and quasi-one-dimensional closure reference

published_models.eq8_asymmetric_normalized: Qstar(x) = Qstar_m * exp(-(((x-x_m)*(x-x_i+k))/((x_c-x_m)*(x-x_i)))^2), applied downstream of x_i
published_models.eq11_total_temperature_relation: Tt(x) = Tt0 + integral[x_i to x](Qdot_prime(s) ds)/(mdot*cp)

evidence_boundary: Equations 6, 7, 8 and 11 are text-recoverable and their mathematical forms may be implemented independently of case-specific parameter values.
The paper explicitly states that Q_m, x_m, x_c, x_i and k depend on operating conditions and require prediction/estimation.
Figure-derived Q_m, x_m and x_i values are not digitized or guessed in this repository.
Case-10 x_c=98 and k=5.6 remain raw text records until their coordinate/unit convention is frozen together with x_m and x_i.
A formal solver case still requires an absolute thermal power or an independently measured stagnation-enthalpy rise.

sources.citation: Lu Tian, Lihong Chen, Qiang Chen, Fei Li, Xinyu Chang, Modeling and Measurements of Heat Release Distributions in Dual-mode Scramjet Combustor, 18th AIAA/3AF International Space Planes and Hypersonic Systems and Technologies Conference, 2012, AIAA 2012-5833.
sources.role: independent modified quasi-one-dimensional heat-release inference and TDLAS validation reference

facility_records.multiport_injector: 7 x 1.2 mm sonic ports, 60 mm upstream of each cavity leading edge

confirmed_claims: The modified one-dimensional method inferred axial heat release by matching calculated pressure to measured pressure.
TDLAS temperature and velocity measurements were used as independent checks of the inferred heat-release distributions.
For the single-port case, the one-dimensional model neglects the cavity and agreement at combustor entry/exit is described as more reliable than inside the cavity region.
The paper reports ram-scram transition near the downstream end of the large heat-release region in its modeled cases.
evidence_boundary: The accessible text does not explicitly identify the fuel chemical species or its LHV for these cases, so combustion efficiency and equivalence ratio are not converted into absolute thermal power here.
The fitted axial heat-release profiles are presented graphically rather than as a complete tabulated solver-ready distribution in the accessible text.
No figure coordinates are digitized or guessed as formal inputs.

required_same_case_evidence: source locators for every promoted parameter
explicit source-to-solver axial coordinate mapping in metres
solver-ready axial shape: traceable Eq. 8 parameters or tabulated line heat
absolute heat addition: positive total heat-release power or measured stagnation-enthalpy increment with mass flow
shape and absolute-energy evidence tied to the same declared operating condition
explicitly_forbidden_shortcuts: mixing shape parameters and absolute power from unrelated operating conditions
assuming 100 percent combustion efficiency without source evidence
converting equivalence ratio to power when fuel identity/LHV or oxidizer convention is unresolved
digitizing figures without a retained extraction record and coordinate convention
treating normalized CH* intensity as absolute W/m without an independent energy scale

project_decision.mutual_exclusion: Direct heat_release_rate_per_length and burned-fuel/LHV energy paths may not both be active, preventing double counting.
project_decision.next_evidence_priority: Recover a complete absolute heat-addition level and matching axial shape parameters from one internally consistent published case; do not mix geometry/shape/power from unrelated experiments and label the result as a reproduction.
